slides.narration: Welcome to Book II, Chapter 12: Creating Reusable Generic Classes. This deck follows the Chapter 1 Slides model: concept on the left, code or evidence on the right, and presenter notes that tell the instructor what to say and do. Modern C++ is not about using the newest syntax because it looks impressive. It is about encoding ownership, lifetime, invariants, generic behavior, and failure boundaries so the program is easier to reason about and harder to misuse.

Writing row one, column two updates the sixth element of the flat storage to seven. Row zero, column zero remains zero. slides.title: Failure clinic — One unchecked multiplication
keyPoints: A matrix template computes its storage size with an unchecked product of dimensions.
On a target where that product wraps in the size type, the array can be smaller than the programmer intended.
Later indexing then operates against the wrong representation.
The repair is a representability constraint before multiplication, plus an application-level policy limiting.
slides.narration: In Book II, Chapter 12, treat Failure clinic — One unchecked multiplication as a design decision with costs and evidence. A matrix template computes its storage size with an unchecked product of dimensions. On a target where that product wraps in the size type, the array can be smaller than the programmer intended. Later indexing then operates against the wrong representation. The repair is a representability constraint before multiplication, plus an application-level policy limiting impractically large shapes. Another defect validates only the flat index. An invalid coordinate such as column equal to the column count can accidentally refer to the next row. The index is within the array but the requested coordinate is outside the matrix’s contract. Validate the semantic coordinates, not only the final storage address.
